themes_detail.label: Encampment surge in parks
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.2-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks—a 1,100% increase (z-score: 6.35)—suggesting a rapid emergence of unsheltered populations in Morris Park/Pelham Parkway public spaces.
evidence: 3 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.35 indicates statistically rare spike
Community Board budget requests include 'Enhance park safety through more security staff' (recurring unfunded request)
reporting_angles: On-the-ground reporting: where exactly are encampments appearing, what do residents report, what services exist nearby?
Policy angle: why park safety funding has been chronically underfunded despite repeated CB budget requests; what the city's response timeline looks like

themes_detail.label: Drug activity spike in neighborhood
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints jumped to 5 LAST WEEK versus a 0.4-per-week baseline over 8 weeks—a 1,233% increase (z-score: 6.65)—marking the second-highest-severity spike in the district and potentially signaling organized drug market activity or enforcement gaps.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.65 indicates statistically rare, high-severity spike
No recent local news coverage or Reddit discussion of this issue, suggesting it may be underreported in media
reporting_angles: Precinct and NYPD presence: are there known hot spots, what's the enforcement strategy, have community safety meetings been held?
Resident safety perception: interviews with local business owners, parents, and long-term residents about changes they've noticed

themes_detail.label: Park noise complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Noise-in-park complaints surged to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO compared to a 0.1-per-week baseline—a 2,300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—the highest-scoring spike in the dataset, indicating either major events or chronic management issues in the district's park spaces.
evidence: 3 park noise complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Highest z-score in dataset (8.69) indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Community Board budget requests include 'Reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity' and 'Enhance park safety through more security staff' (recurring themes)
reporting_angles: Event-based reporting: were there specific concerts, gatherings, or events in parks 2 weeks ago that triggered complaints?
Park management angle: do parks have noise ordinances, enforcement mechanisms, or staffing to manage large gatherings?

themes_detail.label: Indoor air quality complaints triple
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints jumped to 7 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a 1.8-per-week baseline over 8 weeks—a 300% spike (z-score: 6.33)—potentially linked to heating system failures, mold, or chemical exposure affecting multiple residences.
evidence: 7 indoor air quality complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.33 indicates high-severity statistical spike
Heat/hot water is the #1 complaint type overall (3,285 in 90 days), suggesting chronic building system failures may be root cause
reporting_angles: Building conditions investigation: which buildings or blocks generated these complaints? Are they rent-stabilized, older housing stock?
Health angle: what symptoms/illnesses residents reported; are there patterns suggesting mold, gas leaks, or HVAC failures?

themes_detail.label: Illegal street vending enforcement uptick
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO compared to a 0.4-per-week baseline—a 700% increase (z-score: 5.42)—suggesting either a sudden rise in street vending activity or heightened enforcement action in the district.
evidence: 3 vendor enforcement complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.42 indicates statistically significant spike
No recent local news or Reddit discussion of vending issues in the district
reporting_angles: Street vending ecosystem: are vendors operating legally, what neighborhoods are affected, do residents support or oppose street vending?
Enforcement policy: is DSNY or Parks enforcement ramping up? What triggered the enforcement action?
